attributes.title: Protocol LOC-1: Open-Source Acoustic Metrology for Testing the Locational Variable Hypothesis in a 230 kHz Hollow Copper Sphere
attributes.description: Preregistered experimental protocol for Project S.P.H.E.R.E. evaluating whether a 99.999% purity hollow copper sphere exhibits a reproducible location-associated acoustic resonance shift above 230 kHz after rigorous environmental and instrumental control.

344-2.value:
Primary Research Question:
Does moving a controlled 99.999% purity hollow copper sphere between specified positions produce a repeatable change in its selected resonance above 230 kHz, relative to a stationary reference sphere, that exceeds a preregistered effect threshold and survives independent replication?Null Hypothesis ($H_0$):
After preregistered environmental, thermal, and mechanical corrections, the location-associated resonance difference between positions A and B lies within the predefined equivalence bounds.Alternative Hypothesis ($H_1$):
A frequency ratio difference exceeding the smallest effect of interest persists across randomized placement returns, survives control experiments, and is independently replicated.

344-4.value: Data does not yet exist. No part of the data that will be used for this analysis plan exists, and no part will be generated until after this plan is registered.

344-14.value: No experimental data, pilot observations, or preliminary unblinded measurements have been gathered, inspected, or analyzed for this confirmatory test. Protocol LOC-1 is strictly an a priori technical specification and experimental design baseline; the project currently operates as a pre-entity, pre-funding research initiative.

value: Adjustment or control-based design: The association between variables is adjusted or controlled for a set of other factors that would otherwise influence the estimation of that relationship. Note that typically this is performed in order to eliminate influences to help isolate some causal effect. If there is a reason other than isolating a causal effect for controlling for variables, please describe it.

Non-randomized study: Does not include random assignment of subjects to treatments or conditions. This usually includes correlational studies, observational studies, surveys, natural experiments, real-world evidence studies, regression discontinuity designs, and descriptive studies.

Direct inference on causal relationship(s): This study is intended to infer or estimate a causal relationship between two or more variables. It is designed specifically for the purposes of causal inference or identification.
Researchers or observers who code or interpret data for analysis will not be aware of the assigned treatments during coding.

344-38.value: Position labels ($A$ and $B$) are cryptographically or numerically coded before data transfer to the primary analyst. The analysis scripts, statistical thresholds, and data pipelines are completely frozen before the position keys are unblinded.

344-40.value: Protocol LOC-1 uses a same-enclosure two-position metrology design with a stationary reference channel.Parameters: Two primary positions ($A$ and $B$) separated by 0.40 m center-to-center within an environmental enclosure, alongside a third fixed position for a stationary reference sphere.Sampling & Blocks: A total of 80 principal placements (40 per position) structured into 10 experimental blocks of 8 placements.Sequencing: Randomized, balanced $A/B$ scheduling within each block, with a default thermal and mechanical settling time of 30 minutes per placement.Measures: High-frequency surface velocity via Laser Doppler Vibrometry (LDV) and complex scattering $S_{11}$ tracking via a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA), paired with continuous 1 Hz environmental telemetry (temperature, pressure, vibration, magnetic field, and Rubidium timebase lock status).

344-44.value: Randomized balanced block scheduling. Within each of the 10 experimental blocks of 8 trials, the order of position presentation ($A$ and $B$) is randomized and balanced to eliminate drift or time-of-day biases.

344-47.value: Data collection follows Protocol LOC-1 specifications using a same-enclosure two-position design ($0.40\text{ m}$ center-to-center separation between position A and position B) and a stationary reference sphere within a controlled thermal and mechanical environment. Each placement requires a default settling time of 30 minutes, continuous environmental logging at $\ge 1\text{ Hz}$ (temperature, pressure, ambient vibration, magnetic field, and Rubidium timebase status), and synchronized acquisition of Laser Doppler Vibrometry (LDV) surface velocity and Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) $S_{11}$ scattering parameters. Full instrumentation parameters and exclusion criteria (such as Rubidium lock loss or temperature excursions exceeding $\pm 0.001\text{ K}$) are detailed in the attached whitepaper.

344-51.value: The sample size consists of 80 principal experimental placements total, divided evenly into 40 placements for Position A and 40 placements for Position B. These are structured into 10 experimental blocks of 8 placements each, incorporating randomized, balanced $A/B$ scheduling. A stationary reference channel operates concurrently across all conditions

344-53.value: The sample size of 40 placements per position (80 total) is chosen to provide sufficient statistical power for detecting frequency ratio differences above the predefined equivalence bounds while balancing operational constraints, thermal stabilization limits, and block-randomization requirements.

344-55.value:
Starting Rules: Pilot testing and hardware qualification (Milestones M0–M3) conclude once environmental stability, baseline noise floors, and fixture repeatability criteria are met and verified. Confirmatory data collection begins only after formal protocol preregistration and freezing of the analysis script.

Stopping Rules: Data collection terminates automatically upon completion of the pre-specified 80 principal placements (10 blocks of 8). Any subsequent data collection is restricted to secondary or exploratory conditions and cannot alter the primary confirmatory dataset

344-58.value: The primary manipulated variable is the spatial position of the primary test artifact within the environmental enclosure, configured as a two-level categorical treatment:   Position A: Primary test location coordinates within the shielded metrology chamber.Position B: Secondary test location coordinates, separated from Position A by a 0.40 m center-to-center displacement.   Control Condition: A stationary reference sphere positioned at a third fixed location remains unmoved throughout all trials to provide a common-mode baseline channel

344-62.value: Primary Outcome Measures: Selected resonance frequencies of the test artifact ($f_T$) and reference artifact ($f_R$), derived from non-contact surface velocity profiles via Laser Doppler Vibrometry (LDV) and complex scattering parameter ($S_{11}$) sweeps via a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA).   Covariates & Telemetry: Continuous environmental and instrumental parameters logged at $\ge 1\text{ Hz}$, including enclosure temperature ($K$), barometric pressure ($Pa$), ambient floor vibration magnitude, magnetic field activity, drive signal amplitude, and Rubidium frequency standard lock status.   Exclusion & Quality Control Variables: Real-time quality flags, Rubidium holdover events, temperature excursions exceeding $\pm 0.001\text{ K}$, and floor vibration threshold breaches used to filter invalid acquisitions prior to unblinding.

344-66.value:
Measured frequency values are combined into normalized performance and contrast metrics:Resonance-Frequency Ratio ($r(t)$): The instantaneous ratio combining test and reference frequency estimates to cancel common-mode drift:$$r(t) = \frac{f_T(t)}{f_R(t)}$$   Location Contrast in Parts Per Billion ($\Delta_{ppb}$): The standardized difference metric computed between positional blocks:$$\Delta_{ppb} = 10^9(\bar{r}_A - \bar{r}_B)$$
where $\bar{r}_A$ and $\bar{r}_B$ represent the mean frequency ratios for positions A and B, respectively.   Combined Standard Uncertainty ($u_c(y)$): Evaluated via a linearized measurement model incorporating partial derivatives and covariance matrices to account for shared thermal and timebase influences:$$u_c^2(y) = \sum_{i}\left(\frac{\partial g}{\partial x_i}\right)^2u^2(x_i) + 2\sum_{i<j}\frac{\partial g}{\partial x_i}\frac{\partial g}{\partial x_j}\text{cov}(x_i, x_j)$$

344-71.value:
Model Type & Specification:
A linear mixed-effects model and block-structured ANOVA incorporating explicit treatment of block structure and serial dependence (residual autocorrelation). The model evaluates the location contrast metric ($\Delta_{ppb} = 10^9(\bar{r}_A - \bar{r}_B)$) across positional blocks while incorporating environmental covariates (temperature, barometric pressure, vibration) and shared timebase calibration terms.   Equivalence Testing:
A Two One-Sided Tests (TOST) procedure is implemented to test equivalence against the pre-specified smallest effect of interest.   Controls & Assumptions:
Negative controls include stationary reference sphere measurements, dummy artifact runs, and sham positional moves. Model assumptions (residual normality, homoscedasticity, and autocorrelation) will be verified via residual diagnostics prior to unblinding

344-75.value:
Categorical Variables:
Spatial position is coded as a binary indicator variable ($A$ vs. $B$).Data Transformation & Centering:
Raw frequency estimates are transformed into the normalized frequency ratio $r(t) = f_T(t) / f_R(t)$ and scaled into parts-per-billion ($\Delta_{ppb}$) contrast values. Continuous environmental covariates (temperature, pressure) are mean-centered relative to baseline operating setpoints.

344-77.value:
Significance Level:
Primary confirmatory hypothesis testing is conducted using a two-sided test at a significance threshold of $\alpha = 0.01$.   Equivalence Bounds:
Evaluated against pre-specified equivalence bounds established during hardware qualification milestones.   Multiple Testing:
Confirmatory primary endpoints are strictly separated from secondary and exploratory analyses, which are reported independently

344-79.value:
Inclusion Criteria:
All completed principal placements (40 per position, 80 total across 10 balanced experimental blocks) satisfying all real-time quality control flags.   Exclusion Criteria:
Placements flagged by automated quality filters—including Rubidium timebase lock loss, temperature excursions exceeding $\pm 0.001\text{ K}$, floor vibration threshold breaches, or uncalibrated drift—are excluded prior to unblinding in accordance with preset protocol rules. Outliers resulting from equipment transients are dropped strictly according to these pre-established exclusion rules.

344-81.value:
Handling Strategy:
Models will be conducted on complete cases meeting all quality and inclusion criteria. Incomplete or corrupted records due to transient sensor dropouts will be omitted from paired block comparisons rather than statistically imputed, and any data loss will be explicitly recorded in the protocol deviation log.

344-83.value:
Exploratory & Secondary Analyses:
Secondary evaluations include frequency-versus-drive-amplitude response sweeps, cross-correlation of fit residuals with environmental telemetry fields, and out-of-band acoustic mode tracking. These exploratory analyses are explicitly segregated from the primary confirmatory test

344-86.value: Project S.P.H.E.R.E. and Protocol LOC-1 operate under an open-science governance model, emphasizing complete methodological transparency, preregistration, open data, and independent replication.   Additional contextual details regarding this research plan include:Evidentiary Distinction: This experimental program strictly evaluates established engineering metrology (laser vibrometry, VNA scattering analysis, rubidium timebase referencing, and environmental controls). It separates measurable physical parameters from speculative background hypotheses or unverified operational claims.   Open Access & Provenance: All protocol documentation, versioned whitepapers, and future raw datasets are archived with persistent identifiers on Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23583932), complemented by open-source repositories on GitHub and simulation tools via the SPHERE portal (spheredesci.org).Commitment to Disclosure: In accordance with project governance standards, all findings—including confirmatory null results or inconclusive outcomes—will be fully published within 60 days of unblinding.
